prompt: True or false: according to OSIsoft, a PI Data Archive collective with daily PI Backups is a complete disaster recovery solution.

options.text: True
False

explanation: False. OSIsoft states "PI Backups, Redundant Interfaces and High Availability are NOT stand-alone Disaster Recovery solutions", and recommends a DR simulation at least once a year.

prompt: Put the steps for moving an archive file to a new disk in order.
explanation: The 2017 R2 course: force a shift, unregister, move the .arc and .ann files, then re-register. The .ann file must stay in the same directory as its archive.

prompt: Why can users on the secondary not see the restored period?

options.text: piartool changes archive registration only on the host it runs on, and archives are independent on each member
Secondaries never store archives
The archive must be registered in AF first
The secondary needs a reboot to replicate it

scenario: On a two-member collective, an admin runs piartool on the primary to register a restored archive. Users querying the secondary still cannot see that period.
explanation: "You need to run piartool on the PI Data Archive host which you want to modify the archive registration on." Archives are independent per member; only some configuration replicates.

prompt: How can PI Backup back up archive files that are in use without stopping the Data Archive?

options.text: It uses Windows Volume Shadow Copy Service (VSS)
It pauses the snapshot subsystem for an hour
It reads only the event queue
It copies files from a secondary instead

explanation: PI Backup uses VSS, so it can back up files in use without downtime.

prompt: What backup approach does AVEVA's UC23 security deck recommend for ransomware recovery?

options.text: Daily off-peak backup locally, then copy it to a separate server or network drive
Weekly backup to the same disk as the archives
Rely on the collective secondary instead of backups
Back up only the license file

explanation: Schedule daily off-peak backups with Task Scheduler, back up locally, then copy to a separate server or network drive. Leaving backups only on the same server is a listed pitfall.

prompt: 99.9% uptime allows about how many hours of downtime per year?
explanation: 99.9% uptime allows about 43.8 minutes per month, or 8.76 hours per year.

prompt: How does PI Collective Manager synchronise a new secondary?

options.text: It takes a PI Backup of the primary, copies it and registers it on the secondary
It streams every event from the primary since install
It copies only the license file
It rebuilds archives from the interface buffers

explanation: Collective Manager synchronises a secondary by taking a PI Backup of the primary, copying it and registering it.

prompt: Per a 2025 AVEVA feedback idea, what does moving a PI Data Archive to a new server currently require?

options.text: Installing the same software version and restoring from a backup of the old server
Copying the PI folder to the new server and starting services
A built-in live migration wizard
Exporting all points with AFExport

explanation: The feedback idea says the move requires installing the same version, then restoring from a backup. There is no live migration wizard, and AFExport is for AF databases.

prompt: The course says to keep at least how many empty historic archive files?
explanation: Keep at least 2 empty historic archive files so archive shifts always have somewhere to go.

prompt: Which uses of backup copies does the 2026 PI System Software Schedule forbid? Select all that apply.

options.text: Testing or training
A hot standby
A caching server
Restoring after a failure

explanation: Backup copies may not be used for testing or training, "as a hot standby" or "as a caching server". Restoring is what a backup is for.

prompt: What is the main step to repoint the data references to the production Data Archive after import?

options.text: Change the one Data Archive Name attribute to the production server
Edit each data reference individually
Rename the production server to match test
Re-run AFImport with /Security

scenario: You are promoting an AF database from a test environment to production. In test, all PI Point data references use the server path %@\Data Archive|Name%.
explanation: With substitution parameters, editing one Data Archive Name attribute repoints all linked attributes during a migration.

prompt: What trade-off did OSIsoft note for restoring Azure PI VMs from disk snapshots?

options.text: Much faster than redeploying, but snapshots are large, not portable and must restore to the same environment
Slower than redeploying but portable to AWS
Free and unlimited
Only works for the domain controller

explanation: The Azure deployment deck says restoring from disk snapshots is much faster than redeploying, but snapshots are large, not portable and must restore to the same environment.
